cases.sentence: – Вот он, – сказал ___, указывая на Левина, – он тут главное лицо.
cases.explain: «старый князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Here he is,” said the old prince, pointing to Levin—“he’s the principal person in the matter.”

cases.sentence: – А я? – сказала она. – Даже тогда… – Она остановилась и опять продолжала, решительно глядя на него своими ___, – даже тогда, когда я оттолкнула от себя свое счастье.
cases.explain: «правдивыми глазами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “And I!” she said. “Even when. …” She stopped and went on again, looking at him resolutely with her truthful eyes, “Even when I thrust from me my happiness. I always loved you alone, but I was carried away. I ought to tell you. … Can you forgive that?”

cases.sentence: Потом приехали родные, и начался тот блаженный сумбур, из которого Левин уже не выходил до ___ своей свадьбы.
cases.explain: «другого дня» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Their conversation was interrupted by Mademoiselle Linon, who with an affected but tender smile came to congratulate her favorite pupil. Before she had gone, the servants came in with their congratulations. Then relations arrived, and there began that state of blissful absurdity from which Levin did not emerge till the day after his wedding. Levin was in a continual state of awkwardness and discomfort, but the intensity of his happiness went on all the while increasing. He felt continually that a great deal was being expected of him—what, he did not know; and he did everything he was told, and it all gave him happiness. He had thought his engagement would have nothing about it like others, that the ordinary conditions of engaged couples would spoil his special happiness; but it ended in his doing exactly as other people did, and his happiness being only increased thereby and becoming more and more special, more and more unlike anything that had ever happened.

cases.sentence: Он посоветовался со ___ и, получив его разрешение, передал Кити свой дневник, в котором было написано то, что мучало его.
cases.explain: «старым князем» — after the preposition «со», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The confession he had promised was the one painful incident of this time. He consulted the old prince, and with his sanction gave Kitty his diary, in which there was written the confession that tortured him. He had written this diary at the time with a view to his future wife. Two things caused him anguish: his lack of purity and his lack of faith. His confession of unbelief passed unnoticed. She was religious, had never doubted the truths of religion, but his external unbelief did not affect her in the least. Through love she knew all his soul, and in his soul she saw what she wanted, and that such a state of soul should be called unbelieving was to her a matter of no account. The other confession set her weeping bitterly.

cases.sentence: Левин не без ___ передал ей свой дневник.
cases.explain: «внутренней борьбы» — after the preposition «без», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Levin, not without an inner struggle, handed her his diary. He knew that between him and her there could not be, and should not be, secrets, and so he had decided that so it must be. But he had not realized what an effect it would have on her, he had not put himself in her place. It was only when the same evening he came to their house before the theater, went into her room and saw her tear-stained, pitiful, sweet face, miserable with suffering he had caused and nothing could undo, he felt the abyss that separated his shameful past from her dovelike purity, and was appalled at what he had done.

cases.sentence: – Возьмите, возьмите эти ___! – сказала она, отталкивая лежавшие пред ней на столе тетради. – Зачем вы дали их мне!..
cases.explain: «ужасные книги» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Take them, take these dreadful books!” she said, pushing away the notebooks lying before her on the table. “Why did you give them me? No, it was better anyway,” she added, touched by his despairing face. “But it’s awful, awful!”

cases.sentence: Нет, все-таки лучше, – прибавила она, сжалившись над его ___. – Но это ужасно, ужасно!
cases.explain: «отчаянным лицом» — after the preposition «над», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Take them, take these dreadful books!” she said, pushing away the notebooks lying before her on the table. “Why did you give them me? No, it was better anyway,” she added, touched by his despairing face. “But it’s awful, awful!”

cases.sentence: Однако счастье его было так велико, что это признание не нарушило его, а придало ему только ___.
cases.explain: «новый оттенок» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: But his happiness was so immense that this confession did not shatter it, it only added another shade to it. She forgave him; but from that time more than ever he considered himself unworthy of her, morally bowed down lower than ever before her, and prized more highly than ever his undeserved happiness.
